windowTitle: Serial integration - stage 1 reconcile origin/main interleaving and restore the W08 Capability COS overlay
scope: Reconcile the four-domain branch with origin/main (PRs #684 build registry redirect, #686 deployment-unit docs, #688 CloudIdentity readiness, #689 capability COS storage/storage-provider) without blindly replacing either side, then restore the W08 Capability acceptance behaviours the canonical #689 base did not carry. No provider, wallet, production or Instance action.
decisions: services/internal/ownerservice/bootstrap.go and services/build/internal/build/runner.go were byte-identical on both sides (#688/#684), so the merge kept a single copy with no conflict.

The capability byte plane had two parallel implementations: origin/main (#689, canonical) keeps Storage.Assemble plus a separate archive-validated Promote; the branch's pre-final capture did the content-addressed copy inside Assemble. The merge kept origin/main's Promote model as the base, because validation-before-promote is the canonical #689 semantic, and overlaid only the W08 behaviours #689 lacked.

services/gateway-integration/cmd/server/main.go: the merge kept main's peer loop and re-added the branch's GatewayStore wiring (OPL_GATEWAY_DATABASE_URL branch + gatewaymigrations import + s.GatewayStore); verified by diff vs origin/main showing only the added block.
implemented: services/capability/catalog/storage.go + local_storage.go + cos_storage.go: restored the W08 resume/finalize reconciliation seam - Storage.ListParts plus ProviderParts/ProviderPart, implemented for both the local and the COS provider, so GetUpload only reports the shards the provider actually holds and a resumed upload re-sends only the missing ones.

services/capability/catalog/cos_storage.go: restored the crash-recovery window - Assemble falls back to the content-addressed immutable object (re-verified) when the multipart is gone, and ListParts reports the finalized upload (Complete) instead of failing or starting a second upload identity.

services/capability/catalog/uploads.go: GetUpload reconciles an UPLOADING session through reconcileUploadParts against the registered part identity, without rewriting the owner data-plane observation; CompleteUpload keeps the canonical validation-before-Promote path.

commands: GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly go -C services/capability vet ./... ; go build ./...
GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly go build ./... across all 15 modules; go.mod/go.sum sha256 diff before/after shows no churn
verification.environment: local loopback PostgreSQL container for the owner-migration tests; no other external dependency
cases: TestGetUploadReconcilesDirectProviderShardsForResume (capability): a real isolated PostgreSQL Capability owner over a real COS-provider fake; GetUpload reports exactly the shard the provider holds, reconciliation does not rewrite the owner observation, cross-tenant readback is refused, a never-received shard is not reported.

TestCompleteUploadFinalizesDirectProviderUploadAndReadsBack / TestCompleteUploadRecoversArtifactCopiedBeforeOwnerCommit: finalize reads back; the crash window (validated bytes copied to the content-addressed key before the owner commit) is recovered from the immutable object.

TestCOSAssembleRecoversCopiedImmutableObjectAfterCrash / TestCOSRecoveryReVerifiesTheImmutableObject / TestCOSListPartsReconcilesMidUploadShards: the COS provider itself, over real SDK request/response shapes, recovers the copied artifact, re-verifies (tamper -> digest mismatch), fails closed for an unknown finalized upload, and reports exactly the mid-upload shards.

notRun: No real Tencent COS bucket, TCR, Sub2API, provider purchase, real charge, route mutation, Candidate build, Instance deployment or production readback.
docs/spec/target checks and npm run verify:local:full were not rerun in this slice; they are the stage-6 obligation and no machine contract/schema/spec-validation input changed in this merge.
claimBoundary: This receipt claims the origin/main interleaving merge and the restored W08 Capability COS resume/recovery source behaviours, proven by focused module builds and isolated-PostgreSQL COS-provider tests. It claims no deployment, no provider or wallet action, no Candidate and no production acceptance.
secrets: none: no credentials, tokens, keys, customer data or private addresses.
